Cross-cutting · Strength / shrinkage / creep / cracking / thermal behavior

812 resources · Last updated November 20, 2026

What's new Topics Key issues Resources Research gaps Change log Get updates Reactions Calculator

Key points

  • Partial coverage: Strength, curling, plastic shrinkage and mass heat have distinct mechanisms; broad creep and shrinkage constitutive models remain gaps.
  • Pass 3: Hillerborg 1976 fictitious crack model, Modéer 1979 Lund thesis, Bažant–Oh crack band (1983), van Mier multiaxial softening thesis (1984), Brincker 1989, Wittmann 1983, Bažant–Li creep-model comparison (2008), C-S-H nanoscale creep, concrete at elevated temperature (R278, R279, R281, R287, R289, R303, R305, R309, R324, R347, R348, R349, R350, R351, R352, R353, R354, R365).
  • Nov 20 backfill: fracture and size effect (Bažant 2019 book, Kaplan 1961, Hillerborg-era notch sensitivity, Griffith criterion), strain-rate effects in compression and tension, multiaxial and confined stress–strain models (Mander-type, FRP-confined), fatigue of plain and fibre-reinforced concrete, autogenous and drying shrinkage, creep/relaxation (R3562–R4037, 117 records). DOI/abstract level only.
